context: 8. Conclusion We have shown that for wide two-layer ReLU neural networks, training both layers or only the output layer leads to very different implicit biases. When training both layers, the classifier converges to a max-margin classifier for a non-Hilbertian norm, which enjoys favorable statistical properties. Interestingly, this problem does not seem to be directly solvable with known convex methods in high dimension. Proving complexity guarantees for this non-convex gradient flow is an important open question for future work. In particular, even for infinite width, continuous time dynamics as in Theorem 3, it is still unknown whether a convergence rate can be given under reasonable conditions. 12 I MPLICIT BIAS OF WIDE TWO - LAYER NEURAL NETWORKS
